correctness.rationale: On a neighborhood of a regular initial condition the whole finite itinerary is fixed. Each Bayesian update is a coordinate translation by −log γ in log-odds, so the belief-space Jacobian is the stated positive diagonal endpoint ratio. Each numerator is at most 1/4, which bounds every singular value uniformly in the horizon at that initial state. The log of the logistic derivative differs from minus the absolute log-odds by a bounded amount, giving both versions of the coordinate exponent. In the sharpness example the horizon-dependent initial log-odds are T log γ and the final belief is exactly 1/2; fixing any one initial point instead gives exponent log γ<0. The example rules out uniform asymptotic nonpositivity or a uniform vanishing upper bound over initial states, not every finite positive upper bound. All conclusions are branchwise, not estimates across switching boundaries.
residual_risks: Finite arithmetic diagnostics are not an audit or proof of the asymptotic claim. No derivatives at switching boundaries or with perturbation-dependent activation are established.

value.rationale: Distinguishing tangent growth at a chosen horizon from asymptotic sensitivity and from cross-branch separation is useful clarification. As a mathematical finding the proposed refinement is a routine simplification of a published diagonal product, followed by a scalar inverse and a bounded logistic correction; no additional independent invariant or switching result is established.
